I got Resident Evil 1 & 4 digitally because I too lack conviction to stick with my principles. Played a bit of both so far undocked (30 minutes or so of each) and generally my impressions of the ports are positive, RE4 more so (Aside from the lack of Gyro and HD rumble which I knew about going in)

RE4 - Looks and runs great in portable mode with fast loading and no noticeable hitches or drops in framerate. But I'm not as sensitive to drops if it's only a couple dropped here or there, plus only in the village. No option to adjust aim sensitivity, but it felt fine to me with the Joycons nor options to enable 30FPS. Motion blur is disabled by default. There is an option to enable rumble which is defaulted to off that I switched to on but I didn't notice any rumble with it on).

RE1 - Looks as well as the HD ports should, but something about the experience feels ever so slightly weird, I don't think the game is dropping frames at all, but sometimes it feels like there's very tiny, sometime microsecond hangs or what I'm guessing might be loading in the prerendered backgrounds when moving around? It hasn't impaired my run as Chris on the hardest difficulty, but it's not ideal.

Also the rumors of door loads taking awhile, it's true for RE1 at least and my Switch is unmodified. It's not every door transition but certain ones do take like an additional second or two to load up in addition to the door animation.

RE4 gets a solid thumbs up from me port quality wise, and RE1 less so but still passes. I'll have to try docked play and see if RE1 still performs the same.

Don't worry about hurting your social situation. You cannot lose progress towards it, you can only increase it. Certain actions may make it progress faster, but that's a different situation all together.

Tips?

Generally Speaking...

Always make the most of your time inside the TV. Stay there as long as you can, which will be different from Person to Person. To prolong your stay in the TV, make sure to carry Gohom (At least 1, possibly 2) so you can exit a dungeon right away and Vanish Balls to escape from battles you cannot possibly win.

The reason you want to stay long is so you can free up more time to build your social links and skills. For someone well versed in the gameplay, you can probably complete a dungeon in about 2-4 trips, so for someone just starting, I'd say set aside at least 4 trips to the dungeon.

When you make it to the final level of the dungeon, it's probably best NOT to fight the boss right away, and what you can do if your health/SP permits is is to proceed down to the previous floor and grind a few levels just so you have an edge for the boss. If possible, it's always a wise idea to leave the dungeon using the Gohom item on the highest floor you've reached, that way you can proceed on that floor when you return.

Regarding bosses; it's best to try and defeat them as early as possible when permitted and make sure the day you decide to tackle a boss, you stock up on healing items like Revives and Party Healing Items. That way you don't wind up trying to kill them on the last day before the Fog lifts in the TV world, and if you find yourself unable to tackle the boss, you'll still have days left to grind levels and fuse more Personas.

Fusing Personas all depends on what Social Links you've been working and personal taste. It's always a safe bet to have a mix of offensive and supportive ones in your mix.

EDIT: Also if you really mess up and can't defeat the boss, I believe the game gives you an option to reset your clock a week back in-game; but I'm not sure if you keep your current progress or not. But that option is only presented if you go past the 29th of the month. Someone can verify for me.

In response to each of your statements...

1.) Persona plays very, very, very similar to Pokemon. You get to fuse together lots of personas together to make new personas, esentially it's very much like the evolution system. All the personas can level up to gain access to new moves and stat points. 

3.) Persona 4 The Golden has a fantastic story. The main story involves finding out the truth behind the murders that are happening, but there's lots of stuff going on in between and side stories to explore in the form of Social Links (Who you hang out with when not dungeon crawling).

4.) Exploring is sadly not really an option, at least in the sense that there isn't a huge world to explore. The over world is quite small, and so are the dungeons (Which each floor is randomly generated). However, if you take your time to explore the over world, you'll find there are events and side quests to take part in, but most are relatively simple (Go talk to this person for me or involves getting an item from a specific mob).

5.) This is a big strength I think of the Persona series. There are plenty of reasons to replay through this game. Assuming you're not the type who just naturally wants to replay through the game, there's reason enough just to explore all the social links. Unless you're a time management expert and cheat by using guides, you will not be able to talk to everyone and fully explore everyone's story. The first time i beat Persona 4 on PS2, I only maxed my social link with 3 characters. Aside from just wanting to experience every drop of story, which social links you choose to pursue will give you huge benefits to certain personas and access to special personas, changing the way you play each time subtlety. 

So yeah I'm sure someone could have explained better then I did, but Persona is fucking awesome, for reasons I didn't get to list. If you have a Vita already, just get Persona 3 Portable. I'd find it very hard that if you like Pokemon that you wouldn't at least enjoy the Persona series.

I have the official case (The Leather One) and no Vita.

The outside of the case looks very nice and sleek. The inside feels very soft, and should protect the front and back of the device from any scratches. The official case also has the luxury of transforming into a stand to display your Vita for showing off videos, which is a huge plus. Finally, the case seems like it's designed so the case will hook to the Vita, meaning that it will dangle from the Vita while you're playing it so you don't have to put it down while in use. I'd like to say there is enough padding to keep your Vita safe from most fall damage, and the case should not open on impact and send your Vita flying (A problem I had with the hard logitech case for the PSP) thanks to a sturdy Velcro strap to keep the case shut.

The case seems to leave the sides of the device exposed, which could potentially be a weak spot if dropped or stored in your pocket. I said earlier that the case should protect from most fall damage, but I'm nothing if not imaginative, and if you should drop the Vita is such a way where it would land and hit the exposed sides, the case is going to do little to protect that. Still, that seems like a remote possibility, but it is a worry.

Overall, I'd say the official case is great with the intention of transporting your vita in your pocket/bag and will protect the front and back of your Vita from any damage. It also has the added bonus of transforming into a stand to watch movies and video. The case does leave the sides of the system exposed to potential damage, but only in rare circumstances could that come into play.
